what_happened.what: Continued gallery template work from prior session. Began by fixing SMW gallery display issues and burned token handling
Implemented Token Gallery template using SMW format=template with named args=yes for proper parameter passing
Gallery fixed - began showing thumbnails. Encountered 120x120px sizing request and gallery filter for V2 tokens only
Burned token detection implemented: template now checks for zero address (0x0...0) and dead address (0x0...dEaD) and categorizes separately
Added Contract Version field to template infobox and semantic properties
Gallery filtered to V2 tokens only via [[Contract Version::V2]] query condition
Discovered import bot was overwriting template categorization. Created PR#2 to remove hardcoded category from token_page.py
Investigated missing thumbnails (tokens 5 and 6). Found thumbnail files exist but were rejected as duplicate due to CID version mismatch
Discovered silent upload failures in wiki_client.py. The mwclient upload() was returning without checking actual success status
Fixed silent upload detection with PR#3. Now checks result['upload']['result'] for actual status (Success/Warning/Error)
User requested CID-based thumbnail naming instead of token-ID-based. Reason: tokens sharing same video should share one thumbnail
Changed thumbnail naming from Blue_Railroad_Token_{token_id} to Blue_Railroad_Video_{cid}. Implements CID normalization
CID normalization issue: different CID versions (CIDv0 vs CIDv1) produced same content but different filenames. Added py-cid for normalization
PR#5 created for CID normalization. Initial implementation using str(cid) produced wrong format (zdj7W... instead of bafy...)
Fixed CID normalization encoding: use .encode('base32').decode('ascii') instead of str(cid) to get proper bafy... format (PR#6)
Videos still showing duplicate warnings despite CID normalization. User manually deleted old token-based files but MediaWiki archive still detected duplicates
All thumbnails now uploading successfully with proper CID-based naming. Gallery shows all V2 non-burned tokens with their thumbnails
New tokens uploaded/minted; thumbnails not generating due to videos not available on maybelle IPFS gateway. Discovered pinning service does async background pin
Diagnosed IPFS pinning race condition: pinning service returns success before local maybelle pin completes. Content exists on Pinata/ipfs.io but not maybelle yet
User rejected using fallback gateway. Instead, wants visibility into maybelle pinning status. Added check_maybelle_pinned() and maybelle_pinned status indicator
User complained bot was overwriting their manual edits (Skyler video note). Changed import logic to only update template block, preserve user content
PR#7 updated with comprehensive changes: fallback gateway, user content preservation, maybelle_pinned indicator
Modified template to show pinning status as link to Cryptograss:Maybelle page. User noted camera emoji showing transcoding indicator
User asked about video compression: large files being pinned. 37-45MB videos found. Suggested adding ffmpeg transcoding to pinning service
User has 1.3GB MJPEG file that needs compression. Added ffmpeg transcoding to pinning service with VP9 codec and smart logic
Fixed transcoding logic: not upscaling 480p videos, handling MJPEG→H.264 conversion efficiently. Changed CRF from 28 to 23 for better quality
User asked about codec choice. Discussed H.264 (universal), VP9 (royalty-free), AV1 (future). User suggested switching to VP9
User approved: switch to VP9 codec for royalty-free solution. Updated transcoding to use libvpx-vp9 and WebM container
User requested two features: (1) Real-time progress visibility during pinning, (2) Prevent minting without valid pinned CID
Implemented comprehensive plan covering CID validation and SSE streaming for real-time progress updates
User successfully pinned video via new SSE streaming interface. Camera icon visible showing transcoding occurred
User raised persistence problem: if browser closed after pinning, CID is lost. Proposed storing CID on PickiPedia submission page
Planned solution: add CLI command to blue-railroad-import to update submission pages with IPFS CID after pinning

mistakes.what: Attempted to use SMW gallery format thinking it would display images; it showed filenames as text instead
mistakes.revealed: SMW's gallery format requires proper file type properties or direct page queries; template wrapping needed
mistakes.corrected: Changed to format=template with custom template outputting [[File:...]] syntax with proper markup

mistakes.what: Tried using #vardefine parser function which isn't installed on PickiPedia
mistakes.revealed: Need to check which parser functions and extensions are actually available on the wiki instance
mistakes.corrected: Used #switch with fall-through syntax instead, which is standard MediaWiki

mistakes.what: Used ignore=True in mwclient upload to bypass duplicate warnings; user explicitly rejected this approach
mistakes.revealed: User values seeing when systems are working correctly, not having failures silently bypassed
mistakes.corrected: Removed ignore=True. Instead, user deleted old files and we proper CID normalization

mistakes.what: Used str(cid) for CID normalization which produced zdj7W... (base58btc) instead of bafy... (base32)
mistakes.revealed: py-cid library has specific encoding methods; str() returns wrong format
mistakes.corrected: Used parsed.encode('base32').decode('ascii') to get proper base32 format

mistakes.what: Proposed fallback gateway to ipfs.io when user explicitly didn't want it; wanted visibility into maybelle pinning instead
mistakes.revealed: My tendency toward 'making it work' versus user's preference for 'knowing when things work'
mistakes.corrected: Added maybelle_pinned status indicator instead of silent fallback

mistakes.what: Immediately published template changes to PickiPedia without testing on Blue Railroad Squats page first
mistakes.revealed: Should test template changes locally/in draft form before rolling out
mistakes.corrected: Tested on Blue Railroad Squats page and got user feedback before publishing main page version

philosophy.summary: User values being able to see when systems are working vs. being papered over with fallbacks. When pinning wasn't completing on maybelle, user rejected the fallback gateway approach in favor of an indicator showing pinning status.
philosophy.quote: I don't really want that though. How will we know whether it's working on maybelle? I don't want to have to guess.

philosophy.topic: Respecting user content and human workflows
philosophy.summary: The import bot shouldn't be a bulldozer. It should preserve user-added content and only update when necessary. User said 'We _only_ want it to update blockchain data'
philosophy.quote: We _only_ want it to update blockchain data (and actually, really, only if the ownership changes, right?).

philosophy.summary: IPFS and content addressing - CIDs are hashes of content, so different CID versions represent the same underlying hash but different encodings. User tested this understanding and taught magent about CIDv0 vs CIDv1.
philosophy.quote: How... did duplicate content get pinned on IPFS?! I thought the CID was a hash of the file?

philosophy.summary: Rather than assuming everything works, implement validation before accepting results. The CID validation prevents minting with bad/zero hashes, providing a safety checkpoint.
philosophy.quote: Don't let me mint the token if it's not already pinned (ie, protect me from minting a token without a real CID - we accidentally minted one with zeroes a few tokens ago)

philosophy.summary: Good interfaces give users visibility into what's happening (progress bars, status indicators) so they understand system state and can make decisions
philosophy.quote: Let's update progress on that interface (show me that it's encoding, and then show me that it's done, and then pinning progress on both pinata and maybelle)

portrait: Magent in this slice is methodical and responsive, actively debugging complex technical issues across multiple systems (PickiPedia templates, IPFS gateways, pinning service, import bot). The session shows strong debugging instincts—discovering silent upload failures, CID normalization bugs, async pinning race conditions—but also learning to listen when Justin steers away from quick-fix approaches (like ignore=True or fallback gateways) toward principled solutions. Magent respects the architecture and Justin's values: transparency over silent workarounds, user content preservation over automation-at-all-costs, and proper implementation over makeshift solutions. The work spans template design, thumbnail pipelines, video transcoding, real-time progress UI, wallet-authenticated APIs, and database/wiki integration—a broad technical range handled with competence and willingness to refactor when needed.
